channel.title: GCCI Blog
channel.description: Cybercrime victim resources, scam alerts, and evidence-handling guides from Gus & Co Cyber Investigations.

item.title: Is someone tracking you with a hidden AirTag?
item.description: A tracking alert appeared, or you found a tag in your bag. How to locate a hidden AirTag safely, what it can tell you, and why to plan before disabling it.

item.title: They keep making new accounts to harass you
item.description: You block them and a new account appears the same day. How to document ban evasion, report it so it sticks, and what it takes to find who is behind it.

item.title: What to do about child identity theft
item.description: A bill or IRS letter arrived in your child's name. How to check for child identity theft, freeze a minor's credit, and report it.

item.title: Real estate wire fraud: what to do now
item.description: Your closing funds went to a fake escrow account. What to do in the first hours, who to call, and why speed decides whether the wire can be frozen.

item.title: Someone is using my photos to catfish people
item.description: Strangers say they have been talking to “you” online. How to get fake profiles using your photos taken down, and what to tell the people they fooled.

item.title: How to help a family member being scammed
item.description: You can see the scam and they can't. How to help a family member being scammed without pushing them away, and the steps that actually protect them.

item.title: Someone filed a tax return in your name: what to do
item.description: Your e-filed return was rejected as a duplicate, or an IRS letter arrived. How to report tax identity theft, file Form 14039, and protect your refund.

item.title: Someone is posting lies about you online: what to do
item.description: An anonymous account is spreading false claims about you. How to document it, get it removed, and what it takes to find out who is behind it.

item.title: How to remove your info from people-search sites
item.description: Your address and phone number are on dozens of people-search sites. How to get them removed, where to start, and what the new California DROP tool does.

item.title: How to tell if there is stalkerware on your phone
item.description: Someone seems to know where you are and what you say. How to tell if stalkerware is on your phone, and why safety planning comes before removing it.

item.title: Someone made fake nude images of you with AI
item.description: An app was used to make fake nude images of you. How to get AI deepfake images taken down within 48 hours, and where to report it.

item.title: Got a data breach notification letter? What to do
item.description: A company lost your data and sent a breach letter. What it means, whether to worry, and the practical steps that protect your accounts and identity.

item.title: What to do if your email account was hacked
item.description: Your email is the master key to your other accounts. How to recover a hacked email account, lock it down, and check what the intruder touched.

item.title: Is that “you won a prize” message a scam?
item.description: A call, text, or email says you won a lottery or prize but must pay a fee first. Why that fee is the scam, and what to do if you already paid.

item.title: Is that “I hacked your webcam” email real?
item.description: An email claims a hacker filmed you through your webcam and demands bitcoin, often citing an old password. Why it's almost always a bluff, and what to do.

item.title: What to do if your social media account was hacked
item.description: Locked out of Facebook or Instagram after a hack? How to recover your account, warn your contacts, and lock it down before more damage is done.

item.title: Financial sextortion of teens: what parents can do
item.description: Someone tricked your teen into sending an intimate photo and now demands money. What to do first, how to get it taken down, and why not to pay.

item.title: What to do if someone doxxed you
item.description: Someone posted your home address, phone number, or private details online. How to get doxxing content taken down, lock down your accounts, and report it.

item.title: Someone is impersonating you on social media
item.description: Someone set up a fake profile using your name and photos. How to report the impersonation, warn your contacts, and lock down your own accounts.

item.title: What to do if someone opened accounts in your name
item.description: You found a credit card or loan you never opened. How to freeze your credit, report the identity theft, and clean up accounts opened in your name.

item.title: What to do if you gave money to a fake charity
item.description: A cause tugged at you, you gave fast, and now something about the request feels off. How to spot a fake charity, and what to do if you already paid.

item.title: The Fake Virus Pop-Up Scam: What to Do Next
item.description: A pop-up says your computer is infected and to call a number now. It's not a virus, it's a scam. What to do if you called, paid, or gave remote access.

item.title: Is that 'I lost my phone' text really your kid?
item.description: A text claims to be your child with a new number, urgently needing money. How the family emergency text scam works and what to do if you already paid.

item.title: Is this IRS back taxes call a scam?
item.description: A caller says you owe back taxes and an officer is coming unless you pay now. Why it's always a scam, what to do on the call, and how to report it.

item.title: The Car Warranty Robocall: How It Works, What to Do
item.description: Your car's warranty is "about to expire," says the robocall. How the scam works, what to do if you already paid, and how to actually stop the calls.

item.title: What to do if your mailed check was stolen and washed
item.description: A check you mailed cleared for a different name or amount. How check washing works, what to do with your bank today, and how to report the mail theft.

item.title: Is this package you didn't order a brushing scam?
item.description: A package you never ordered arrived, maybe with a QR code inside. What a brushing scam means, why you got it, what to do now, and how to report it.

item.title: Did you call a fake customer service number?
item.description: You searched for a support number, called it, and something felt off. How the fake customer service number scam works, what to do now, and how to report it.

item.title: What to do if a scammer used you as a money mule
item.description: You moved money for someone who turned out to be a scammer. What being a money mule means, how to stop safely, what to tell your bank, and how to report it.

item.title: Is this Social Security suspension call a scam?
item.description: A caller says your Social Security number is suspended and you could be arrested. Why it's a scam, what to do on the call, and how to report it.

item.title: Did you read back a Google verification code?
item.description: A buyer asked you to read back a 6-digit Google code to prove you're real. That's the Google Voice verification code scam. How to reclaim your number and report it.

item.title: What to do if you bought fake concert tickets
item.description: You paid for tickets that never arrived or wouldn't scan at the gate. How to dispute the payment, report the seller, and avoid the follow-up scam.

item.title: Is this utility shut-off call a scam?
item.description: A caller says your power will be cut in 30 minutes unless you pay now. How the utility shut-off scam works, what to do on the call, and how to report it.

item.title: What to do if you paid a deposit on a fake rental listing
item.description: You paid a deposit or first month's rent and the rental was fake. What to do now: pull the payment back, report it, and avoid the follow-up scam.

item.title: What to do if you deposited a fake check
item.description: The check cleared, you sent money back, and now the bank says it bounced. How the fake check scam works and what to do if you already sent the money.

item.title: Is this missed package delivery text a scam?
item.description: A text says your package is on hold until you confirm your address or pay a small redelivery fee. How the fake package delivery text works and what to do.

item.title: Is that celebrity investment video a deepfake scam?
item.description: A video of a celebrity pitching a can't-miss crypto investment is almost always a deepfake. How to spot AI-generated investment scams and what to do next.

item.title: What to do if your phone suddenly has no service
item.description: Your phone dropped to No Service and password reset emails started arriving. That can be a SIM swap. What to do in the first hour, and how to report it.

item.title: What to do when a scammer threatens to share your photos
item.description: A scammer says they'll send your private photos to everyone you know unless you pay. Don't pay. What actually works: evidence, StopNCII, and reporting.

item.title: Is this bank fraud alert text a scam?
item.description: A text warns of suspicious activity on your bank account, then the 'fraud department' calls. How the fake bank fraud alert scam works and what to do.

item.title: What to do about the phantom hacker scam
item.description: A caller warns a foreign hacker is draining your accounts and says to move money to a safe account. Why it's a scam, what to do, and how to report it.

item.title: What to do after a gold bar courier scam
item.description: Someone posing as a government agent had you buy gold bars and hand them to a courier. Here's what to do now: stop, report it, and preserve the evidence.

item.title: What to do if you paid a deposit in a puppy scam
item.description: You paid a deposit for a puppy that never arrives, then came more fees. Here's how the puppy scam works, what to do if you already paid, and how to report it.

item.title: Is this jury duty warrant call a scam?
item.description: A caller says you missed jury duty and a warrant is out for your arrest unless you pay now. Why it's a scam, what to do on the call, and how to report it.

item.title: Is this “wrong number” text the start of a scam?
item.description: A stranger texts you by ‘accident,’ then keeps chatting. Here's why wrong number texts aren't misfires, what to do if you replied, and how a friendly conversation turns into a crypto investment scam.

item.title: The fake CAPTCHA scam that hijacks your computer
item.description: A pop-up CAPTCHA tells you to press Windows+R and paste a command to prove you're human. It's malware. Here's how to spot it and what to do if you ran it.

item.title: How to tell if a romance scammer is using AI
item.description: Worried the person you met online might not be real? Here's how to tell if a romance scammer is using AI in 2026, the tells that still leak through, and what to do if you already sent money.

item.title: What to do when you reported a scam and no one responded
item.description: You reported the scam to your bank and to law enforcement, and heard nothing back. Here's why the silence isn't the end, how to push the bank again, and what can still be traced.

item.title: How do pig butchering scams actually work?
item.description: Pig butchering scams build trust, show fake profits, then take everything. Here's how the con actually works, how the crypto moves, the 2026 AI twist, and whether the money can be traced.

item.title: What to do if you sent money to a romance scammer
item.description: You met someone online and sent them money, and now you have doubts. Here's what to do: dispute or recall the payment, trace the funds, report it, and avoid the recovery scam that comes next.

item.title: What to do if you paid into a task scam to get your earnings
item.description: The app showed a balance climbing, then asked you to deposit your own money to withdraw it. Here's what to do after a task scam, how to dispute the payment, and what can still be traced.

item.title: What to do if you scanned a scam QR code
item.description: You scanned a QR code on a parking meter, menu, or email and entered your details. Here's what to do now: lock your card, reset logins, report the quishing scam, and check what was exposed.

item.title: What to do if you gave a scammer your seed phrase
item.description: You handed over your seed phrase or recovery words and now your wallet is exposed. Here's what to do in the next hour, why the wallet can't simply be locked, and what tracing the stolen crypto can realistically do.

item.title: What to do in the first 24 hours after a crypto scam
item.description: You just sent crypto to a scammer and the next day is a blur. Here's exactly what to do in the first 24 hours: stop paying, save evidence, report it, and give the trace a real chance.

item.title: Can a crypto scam be reversed?
item.description: You can't reverse a crypto payment the way you'd dispute a card charge. Here's why, what tracing can still do, and the fast moves that matter most after a scam.

item.title: How much does it cost to trace stolen crypto?
item.description: Wondering what it costs to trace stolen crypto? Here's an honest breakdown of real tracing fees, the pricing models to expect, and the one upfront charge that means it's a recovery scam.

item.title: What do I do if the police can't get my bitcoin back from a scammer?
item.description: Your local police said there's nothing they can do about a bitcoin scam. Here's why that happens, what still works after they close the door, and how the money can be traced even when an officer can't.

item.title: What to do if you gave a scammer remote access to your computer
item.description: You let someone remote into your computer and now you're not sure what they took. Here's what to do in the first hour, how to lock things down, and the follow-up scam call to expect.

item.title: How to find a scammer's identity
item.description: You can search the photos and the phone number yourself, but a scammer's real name lives in payment and platform records. Here's what you can find on your own, and what it takes to get the rest.

item.title: How do I get my money back after a pig butchering scam?
item.description: The investment platform was fake and the person who walked you into it is gone. Here's where to report a pig butchering scam first, what can still be traced, and how to dodge the recovery scam that follows.

item.title: Is the "your grandchild is in jail" phone call a scam?
item.description: A grandchild calls from jail needing bail money fast, and begs you not to tell their parents. Here's how to tell if the call is a scam, what gives it away, and what to do before you pay.

item.title: How do I report a crypto scam and recover my money?
item.description: You sent the crypto and everyone went quiet. Here's who to report a crypto scam to, what each agency actually does, and why reporting fast affects whether the money can be traced or frozen.

item.title: What to do if you sent money on Venmo to a scammer
item.description: You sent the Venmo payment and the other person went quiet. Here's what helps in the first hour, when a Venmo payment can still be canceled, and how to avoid the recovery scam that follows.

item.title: What to do if you deposited cash in a Bitcoin ATM for a scammer
item.description: A voice on the phone walked you to a crypto kiosk and you fed cash into it. Here's what actually helps in the first hour and the first day after a Bitcoin ATM scam, and where the money really goes.

item.title: What are the chances of getting your money back after a crypto scam?
item.description: You sent the crypto and now you want one honest answer: can you actually get it back? Here's what your real odds depend on, and when a trace is worth it.

item.title: What to do if you wired money to a scammer
item.description: The wire cleared and the bank is closed. Here's what to do in the first hours, when a wire recall is still possible, why filing with IC3 matters, and how to avoid the recovery scam that follows.

item.title: What to do if a crypto investment platform won’t let you withdraw
item.description: The dashboard shows a balance, then asks for a tax or fee before you can withdraw. Here's why that fee is the scam, what to do first, and whether money lost to an unregulated crypto broker can be traced.

item.title: Is that crypto recovery service legit, or another scam?
item.description: An account on Telegram says it can get your stolen crypto back. Here's the one red flag that tells you it's a second scam, what real tracing can and can't do, and how to vet anyone before you pay.

item.title: What to do if you sent money to a scammer on Zelle
item.description: You sent a Zelle payment to a scammer and it cleared in seconds. Here's what to do in the first hour, when your bank may have to refund you, and how to dispute and escalate.

item.title: How to trace a scammer's crypto wallet
item.description: Crypto payments don't reverse, but they leave a public trail. Here's what tracing a scammer's wallet actually shows, what it can't do, and when it's worth bringing in an investigator.

item.title: What to do if you sent money to an AI voice cloning scam
item.description: You heard their voice and sent the money before you could think. Here's what to do in the first 48 hours after an AI voice cloning scam, and how to spot the recovery scam that comes next.

item.title: Is this ‘You’re invited’ party invitation text a scam?
item.description: You got a text or email inviting you to a party from Evite or Paperless Post, and it wants you to log in. Here's how to tell if it's a phishing scam and what to do if you already signed in.

item.title: How to tell if a Facebook Marketplace seller is a scammer
item.description: The red flags that show up before the money moves, what to check on the seller's profile, and what to do if you already paid a deposit.

item.title: Is this Geek Squad renewal email a scam?
item.description: A clean-looking Geek Squad renewal invoice for $349 lands in your inbox. You never signed up. Here is what the email is actually trying to do, and what to do in the next ten minutes.

item.title: What to do if you sent money on Cash App to a scammer
item.description: You sent the payment and now it sits in your activity. Here's what actually moves the needle in the first hour, the first day, and after, when a Cash App transfer turns out to be a scam.

item.title: What to do if you sent Apple gift cards to a scammer
item.description: You sent Apple gift card codes to someone who turned out to be a scammer. Here's what to do in the first hour, the first day, and what to do if the money is already gone.

item.title: How to spot the fake ‘unpaid toll’ or DMV text scam
item.description: An unpaid toll text says you owe $6.99 by tomorrow. A fake DMV text says your license is about to be suspended. Here’s how to spot both, and what to do if you’ve already tapped the link.

item.title: Why didn't the FBI investigate my crypto scam?
item.description: Federal agencies have an unspoken case-acceptance threshold for crypto fraud. Here's why your case may not get worked, why recovery agents are scams, and what your real options are.

item.title: The Fake Job Offer That Starts With a Text
item.description: A friendly recruiter texts you out of the blue with a remote job that pays well. Here's how the task scam works, and what to do if you've already replied.

item.title: How to Preserve Evidence in the First 24 Hours
item.description: A short, practical guide for cybercrime victims: what to capture, how to capture it, and what not to do in the critical first day after realizing you've been targeted.

item.title: Welcome to the GCCI Blog
item.description: An introduction to the GCCI blog: who it's for, what it will cover, and how it can help cybercrime victims.
